segments.title: Chương 35: 0035【Cái nhìn từ Thịnh Đại】
segments.content:
Magic City.

Shanda Headquarters.

Zhang Yingfeng was reporting on his work.

This Mr. Zhang was in charge of screening, importing, and negotiating all of Shanda's gaming projects, and was also responsible for the authorization, operation, and protection of related copyrights.

In the future, he would rise from Head of Legal Affairs all the way to CEO of Shanda.

A lawyer becoming CEO, aren't you terrified!

Boss Chen sipped his coffee and gestured for Zhang Yingfeng to sit, saying in a good mood, "The higher-ups have already smoothed things over. A special operation will begin on New Year's Day next year. Five ministries and commissions will jointly crack down on private servers and hacks. How's the evidence collection going on your end in the legal department?"

Zhang Yingfeng took out a thick stack of documents. "The main targets are 17173 and 17577."

"17173 was just acquired by Sohu and has transformed into a gaming portal. But they have a huge number of posts involving private server and hack trading. This website won't be easy to deal with. First, they have Sohu backing them. Second, they can shift the blame, saying those are private actions by netizens and the website itself was only negligent in its supervision."

"For 17173, my suggestion is to first send a lawyer's letter, right when the five ministries and commissions launch their special operation. Order them to post a public apology on their homepage, delete all posts involving illegal transactions, and promise to strengthen their management of posts in the future."

"As for 17577, this forum is the most rampant. It's the country's largest base for private servers, openly selling private server frameworks and also selling hacks for Legend and Mir. We must make an example of them and take this forum down. We've already collected a large amount of evidence. But when it comes to specific monetary transactions, we'll need the relevant authorities to gather proof."

"My suggestion is not only to take down 17577 but also to send its webmaster, Can Ying, to jail!"

Boss Chen took the stack of documents and began to look through it seriously.

Zhang Yingfeng summarized, "Private servers and hacks are a never-ending battle. Take one down, and ten more pop up. We need to focus our efforts on gaming forums. That's the root of private servers and hacks. Only by pulling them out by the roots can we solve the problem once and for all. If they lose their platform for distribution, those who run private servers and sell hacks will quickly become like duckweed without roots. After taking down 17577, we'll send lawyer's letters to forums like Ledu, demanding they apologize, delete posts, and strengthen their management."

Zhang Yingfeng's line of thinking was very clear: only go after the roots, not the weeds.

Because there were too many weeds, and you could never get rid of them all; they would grow back with the spring breeze.

But if the roots were gone, the weeds would naturally wither and die.

They talked about a joint operation led by five ministries and commissions, but how much manpower could they really spare to help Shanda?

The entire process, from evidence collection to sentencing, was incredibly long.

By the time a verdict was reached, the special crackdown would have long been over.

Boss Chen gave his directive, "Alright, proceed as you've planned. But sending 17577's webmaster to prison is debatable. There's no need to be so ruthless."

"Chairman, if we don't prosecute them to set a negative example, I'm afraid it won't deter other similar websites," Zhang Yingfeng said.

Boss Chen asked, "Do you have a legal basis?"

Zhang Yingfeng said, "There are no specific laws for this yet, but we can cite copyright-related regulations. It'll be a bit difficult, but we can give it a try."

Trying was useless!

Specific laws had yet to be established. They wouldn't come until 2006. For now, all they could do were administrative measures like this special crackdown.

In other words, it seemed like what Chen Guiliang was doing with his private server was illegal, but in fact, it wasn't.

If he were truly caught by the special task force, he would at most face an administrative fine.

Once the Regulations on the Protection of the Right to Network Dissemination of Information were promulgated in 2006, continuing to run private servers would mean worrying about going to jail.

The very first case of a prison sentence for a private server occurred in 2007, after the legislation was passed. Tianxia Legend had grown to a scale of renting 94 servers and was made an example of by Shanda, who cracked down hard. All five private server partners were arrested.

Boss Chen stated the principle for the operation, "Since the law is ambiguous on this, there's no need to create extra complications. This time, we're cooperating with the five ministries' operation. We must make a strong showing, but we should handle it with a light touch."

Zhang Yingfeng understood. The point was to scare those who didn't know the law, to act as if they were going to send people to prison!

In another timeline, 17577's webmaster, Can Ying, was genuinely scared by Shanda and shut down the website and ran. Later, when he realized nothing would happen, Can Ying resurfaced, but his influence was no longer what it once was.

Boss Chen asked casually, "Did you see those two popular posts recently while you were collecting evidence?"

"The ones about wanting to create a private server that doesn't sell items?" Zhang Yingfeng asked.

Boss Chen nodded.

Zhang Yingfeng said, "Just two players drunkenly boasting, with a large group of players joining in for the fun. No selling point cards, no selling hacks, no selling items. How are they going to make money with their private server? Even if they manage to create it, it'll shut down once their funds run out."

Boss Chen sighed, "The players have a lot of complaints about us. 'Legend refugees,' 'internet orphans'—these have already become buzzwords. I'm afraid even the traditional media will start reporting on it. Sigh, we'll have to spend money on public relations again!"

Some traditional newspapers nowadays loved to report on popular online events.

A single post, a single phenomenon, and the print media could write long-winded articles, even doing a series of reports.

The newspapers got their selling point, and the readers found it novel.

Ever since Legend of Mir exploded in popularity, Shanda had been at the center of a public opinion storm. "Gaming-addicted youth," "electronic opium," and the like had Boss Chen at his wit's end, forcing him to come forward and defend himself on multiple occasions.

Perhaps the public opinion had left some psychological scars on him, causing Boss Chen, who got rich from making games, to look down on the online gaming industry for his entire life.

He felt it wasn't respectable enough and always drew criticism.

The two popular posts created by Chen Guiliang and Tao Chenggang, after breaking out of the online sphere, were like handing weapons to the print media. It was one hundred percent certain that Shanda would be criticized again!

Boss Chen got a headache just thinking about it.

He picked up his coffee again, and Zhang Yingfeng immediately excused himself.

Only one person remained in the office.

Boss Chen sipped his coffee, picked up the mouse, and clicked open the "Private Server Development Log" live text post.

He always felt there was something fishy about this.

He saw the latest update from the poster: "Thanks to the creative idea provided by netizen 'I Wet My Shoes by the River' (a hired poster), Yi Jian Xi Lai and I have decided to adopt his world view..."

"That is, the Marfa continent is facing an invasion by a mysterious power. This mysterious power is the Void Force from the Abyss. The Void Force is causing some of the monsters on the Marfa continent to mutate, and the items dropped by these monsters will also be mutated..."

"To put it plainly, it's just like the old elite monsters and elite items, but we will make the elite monsters particularly powerful, and also make the attributes of the elite items random. Players will have a chance to discover mutated monsters on every map."

"It's possible to kill a scarecrow and get a 'Void Ebony Sword' with stats close to a Purgatory. Moreover, the stats of different 'Void Ebony Swords' will also vary. Every time a player explores a map, it will be like a treasure hunt filled with all kinds of surprises..."

"Thank you again, brothers and sisters, for providing so many suggestions and your selfless support. We will definitely make this private server well. Every monster in the game is the fruit of all our collective efforts!"

Boss Chen carefully read every reply and found that the netizens were acting as if they were on steroids.

The game hadn't even been made yet, but they were already cheering and celebrating.

There were also many netizens offering all sorts of suggestions, even arguing with each other over differing ideas.

At this moment, Boss Chen was very certain that if this private server were to be made, it would inevitably become wildly popular in a short amount of time.

Of course, it would probably be hard to make any money from it. It would be a case of losing money to gain fame.

Because once they started charging, they would face a public opinion backlash.

They promised it would be free!

The more enthusiastic the netizens were now, the more fiercely they would flame when charges were introduced. They would feel betrayed, feel like their emotions had been toyed with, and feel that their youth had been desecrated.

Chen Guiliang could already feel this potential backlash from public opinion.

He had discussed it repeatedly over the phone with Tao Chenggang, Yang Yuhui, and Feng Tao, and they decided to modify the initial game concept to compromise with the emotionally charged netizens.

A ridiculously overpowered private server where you could kill anything in one hit was definitely out of the question.

Chen Guiliang registered an account and made a post to test the waters, suggesting leveling up a few levels with one hit. He was immediately mocked by a crowd of nostalgic old players and flamed by countless people until he couldn't function.

But they couldn't just bow to the players' every whim, or they wouldn't be able to make money.

They could only compromise.

Slightly slow down the leveling speed, slightly lower the level requirement for the Abyss dungeon. Also, increase the number of Void items on normal maps to improve the gaming experience for regular players, while ensuring these items didn't affect their plans for the dungeons.

All the netizens who replied were Chen Guiliang's unpaid game designers. It wouldn't be an exaggeration to call them the godfathers of the private server.

Imperial Capital.

Fu Guoqiang, a Beijing native, was lazing around again today, but he contacted many of his old Legend of Mir buddies, sending them the link to the post via QQ.

His long-lost buddies were filled with emotion after reading the post, and they all replied to the thread to express their feelings.

The original "Legend Refugee Post" had now reached over 9,900 replies and was about to become the third post in Chinese internet history to surpass ten thousand replies—the first was NetEase's "First News Post," and the second was Tianya's "Cairo Declaration Post."

NetEase and Tianya's ten-thousand-reply posts were due to their massive user bases.

Chen Guiliang's "Legend Refugee Post," on the other hand, was sustained entirely by the passion of gamers.

One after another, old players poured out their unforgettable experiences. They even called on their friends, asking them to come and see, and those old friends would come and continue to reply. Eventually, people who knew each other and those who didn't started chatting directly in the thread.

Fu Guoqiang and his friends contributed over a hundred replies. They had long since added each other on QQ, but at this moment, they weren't using QQ to catch up. It seemed as though chatting in the thread had more of a sense of ceremony.

Fu Guoqiang typed out his last sentence in the thread: "If this private server is made, are the old brothers from Guangmang willing to fight again? Reply if you copy!"

"Copy!"

"Copy!"

"Copy!"

"..."

Seeing the stream of "Copy!" replies, Chen Guiliang instantly felt a mountain of pressure.

He had managed to rally the people, but if they became unhappy about paying for the dungeons, the public opinion backlash could directly flame this private server to death!

Tao Chenggang also called, "Damn, I can't bring myself to look at the thread anymore."

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's focus on polishing the game and try to make it as complete as possible."

"Then let's postpone the server launch until next Friday night." Tao Chenggang was also under immense pressure now. For the first time, he was feeling that too much good publicity could be a problem.

He was afraid that tens of thousands of players would be queuing for the private server every day, and then all the queuing players would be cursing Shanda together.
